# Difference-in-Differences in Education Research

<p class="lead">A Practical Workshop on Traditional and Staggered DID, with Hands-on R Applications</p>

**Thursday, October 22, 2026 · 12:00-2:00 PM Eastern**<br>
In person: Norman Hall, Room 2707 · [Register for Zoom](https://ufl.zoom.us/meeting/register/OgvL9_Q2QK-zYuH9BGm9fA)

Learn how to use difference-in-differences (DID) to evaluate education policies and
programs. This hybrid workshop covers traditional and staggered DID designs,
comparison groups, parallel trends, treatment-effect interpretation, and diagnostic
checks. Education examples connect these concepts to an R lab using two-way fixed
effects (TWFE) and staggered DID estimators.

## Workshop Schedule

| Time | Session | Focus |
|---|---|---|
| 12:00-1:00 PM | Lecture | Traditional and staggered DID methods. |
| 1:00-1:30 PM | Hands-on R lab | TWFE and staggered DID estimators with guided practice. |
| 1:30-2:00 PM | Questions & discussion | Interpretation and applications in education. |

Open to graduate students, faculty, researchers, and staff. No prior DID programming
experience is required. Bring a laptop to follow the demonstration and try the R code.

## Workshop Materials

[Start the hands-on R lab](workshop.html) · [Prepare R before the session](workshop.html#setup) ·
[Download the data](data.html) · [Slides](slides.html)

The lab uses two simulated district-year panels, with seven years and no adjustment
covariates. The first has a common treatment start; the second has adoption in Years
5, 6, and 7. All lab graphs and models use raw score points.
